data.title: eClearinghouse is required even though KOHS's checklist never mentions it
data.body_md:
This flipped three times in a week before it was settled against primary sources on 8/26/2026.

1. The FY26 NOFO (Section D.2.A) does **not** exempt NSGP from intergovernmental review: applicants must contact their state's Single Point of Contact under Executive Order 12372, and the only way out is a state having no SPOC.
2. Kentucky's rule is default-on: DLG's eClearinghouse page says all federal program applications in Kentucky are subject to EO 12372 and KRS 45.031 unless the application says otherwise. The NOFO never says otherwise.
3. Kentucky has a SPOC: the State Clearinghouse at the Department for Local Government.

**Why it kept flipping:** the KOHS NSGP Application Submission Checklist lists seven items and eClearinghouse is not one of them, and KOHS's grants page links eClearinghouse only under SHSGP. Both are true and both are irrelevant: KOHS's checklist governs the package emailed to KOHS; the clearinghouse letter is a separate obligation to a different agency. **Absence from a state agency's submission checklist is not absence of the requirement.**

**Registration is not submission.** Opening the DLG Portal account is step one. The project itself still has to be entered for review, state agencies comment, and the comments compile into one clearinghouse letter. File it once the wish list is final: the filing describes the project, and a description written before the budget is settled will drift from what is submitted.

data.title: The eClearinghouse letter goes in the package sent to KOHS
data.body_md:
Confirmed in writing by Cindy Seip, the DLG Program Coordinator and state SPOC, on 9/10/2026: the e-Clearinghouse letter goes **with the federal application**. It is the proof that the mandatory intergovernmental review under Executive Order 12372 has been satisfied. It does not simply sit on file with DLG, even though KOHS's own submission checklist never lists it.

A project that is something other than equipment (a program, or similar) goes out to state reviewers, who have **about 30 days**; the letter follows. Build that month into the schedule, and file only once the wish list is final, because the filing describes the project.

DLG publishes instructions for registering a new e-Clearinghouse account on its website, and Cindy will send them on request.
